ruler-001.note: only medicines that "help the heart pump"; no anatomy
ruler-001.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains how the healthy heart works as a pump with four chambers.

ruler-002.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains the two phases of the blood's journey through the heart and lungs.

ruler-003.note: abbreviation footnotes and a reference title; no definition of HF
ruler-003.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains what heart failure ('weak heart') means, using a comparison with a car engine.

ruler-004.note: abbreviation footnote names HFrEF/HFmrEF, but no ejection-fraction cut-offs
ruler-004.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains the three types of heart failure (HFrEF, HFmrEF, HFpEF) based on the ejection fraction.

ruler-005.note: nothing on coronary disease or heart attack leading to HF
ruler-005.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains how coronary artery disease and a heart attack can lead to heart failure.

ruler-006.note: "Treat the causes of heart dysfunction, such as high blood pressure" - cause named, no mechanism
ruler-006.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains how high blood pressure can lead to heart failure.

ruler-007.note: section title on valvular heart disease and valve repair; no symptoms
ruler-007.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains heart valve disease (narrowed or leaky valves) and its typical symptoms.

ruler-008.note: AF ablation for HF patients (2a); not how AF causes HF
ruler-008.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains how atrial fibrillation can contribute to heart failure.

ruler-009.note: genetic counselling in pregnancy; no definition
ruler-009.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains what cardiomyopathies (heart muscle diseases) are and how they can cause heart failure.

ruler-010.note: "Watch for changes in appetite, weight loss, and muscle wasting"
ruler-010.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains why heart failure can cause a bloated belly and loss of appetite.

ruler-011.note: HFrEF drug classes exist (ACE-I/ARB/ARNI lists) but the top hits are footnotes
ruler-011.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that introduces a module about medicines for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) and explains why it focuses on HFrEF.

ruler-012.note: ARNI: "helps the arteries widen and rid the body of salt. Make it easier for the heart to pump"
ruler-012.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains how ARNIs (for example sacubitril/valsartan) help the heart.

ruler-013.note: ACE inhibitors: "Relax blood vessels. Lower blood pressure. Make it easier for the heart to pump blood."
ruler-013.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains in simple words how ACE inhibitors work.

ruler-014.note: "Beta blockers slow the heart rate, lower blood pressure and may reverse some of the heart damage."
ruler-014.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains how beta-blockers protect the heart in heart failure.

ruler-015.note: MRA: "Help the body get rid of salt and fluids."
ruler-015.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains how MRAs help the body get rid of extra fluid.

ruler-016.note: SGLT2: "Originally used to treat diabetes, these medicines have clear benefits for people with heart failure"
ruler-016.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains SGLT2 inhibitors, which were first developed for diabetes, and how they help in heart failure.

ruler-017.note: MRA stopped if potassium cannot be kept <5.5 "to avoid life-threatening hyperkalemia" (3: Harm, B-NR)
ruler-017.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains why a high potassium level in the blood is dangerous and why it is checked.

ruler-018.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains how a weekly pill organizer helps patients take their heart medicines regularly.

ruler-019.note: "An ICD may stop a dangerous heart rhythm that could cause sudden death by giving an electrical shock"
ruler-019.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains why a doctor may recommend an implantable defibrillator (ICD).

ruler-020.note: single- vs dual-chamber ICD recommendation (I, A); does not explain the difference
ruler-020.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains the difference between a single-chamber and a dual-chamber transvenous ICD.

ruler-021.note: subcutaneous defibrillator as an alternative (IIa, B); no explanation of S-ICD/EV-ICD
ruler-021.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains what an S-ICD or EV-ICD is and how it protects the heart.

ruler-022.note: when a CRT-D is recommended (I, A); not what it does
ruler-022.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains what a CRT-D does for people with heart failure.

ruler-023.note: pocket rinsing before closure; nothing on haematoma
ruler-023.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains what a pocket hematoma after defibrillator surgery is and how it is prevented.

ruler-024.note: patient text: leads go into the heart; nothing on lead problems
ruler-024.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains what can go wrong with defibrillator leads and how it is fixed.

ruler-025.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains why regular defibrillator check-ups are important.

ruler-026.note: "replaced when the battery runs out"; "In about 5-10 years, when the battery..."
ruler-026.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains when and why a defibrillator needs to be replaced.

ruler-027.note: nothing on warning signs before a shock
ruler-027.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains warning signs that a defibrillator shock may be coming and what to do.

ruler-028.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains whether an implantable defibrillator can also work as a pacemaker.

ruler-029.note: aerobic training types (walking, cycling, swimming...) and moderate continuous endurance training
ruler-029.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains what aerobic (endurance) training is and gives examples for heart-failure patients.

ruler-030.note: resistance/strength training 2-3 times a week complements aerobic training (HF; not ICD-specific)
ruler-030.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains simple strength training for people with heart failure or an ICD.

ruler-031.note: balance training for older adults at risk of falls (I, B); flexibility only listed
ruler-031.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains why flexibility and balance exercises help and gives two examples.

ruler-032.note: nothing on medical examinations with an ICD
ruler-032.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains which medical examinations are safe with an ICD and which need a doctor's approval first.

ruler-033.note: nothing on work with an ICD
ruler-033.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains whether people with an ICD can keep working and which jobs need extra caution.

ruler-034.note: nothing on how smoking harms the heart
ruler-034.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains how smoking harms the heart and blood vessels.

ruler-035.note: ask about smoking status; support people who quit in hospital
ruler-035.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that gives practical tips for quitting smoking.

ruler-036.note: alcohol limits (2 glasses men, 1 women); abstinence in alcoholic cardiomyopathy
ruler-036.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains how alcohol affects the heart in heart failure.

ruler-037.note: CPAP in HF with obstructive sleep apnea (2a, B-R); formal sleep assessment (2a)
ruler-037.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains sleep apnea in heart failure and how mask therapy helps.

ruler-038.note: only "talk with your doctor about driving limitations"; no rules
ruler-038.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains the driving rules for private drivers after getting an ICD.

ruler-039.note: peripartum cardiomyopathy named in counselling advice; not defined
ruler-039.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains what peripartum cardiomyopathy is.

ruler-040.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains the main signs of depression that people with heart failure should watch for.

ruler-041.note: nothing defining acute HF or decompensation
ruler-041.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains what acute heart failure and 'decompensation' mean.

ruler-042.note: "signs/symptoms of shortness of breath, swelling, fatigue, and other indicators of worsening HF"
ruler-042.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that lists early warning signs that heart failure is getting worse.

ruler-043.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains when to call the emergency number 112 immediately.

ruler-044.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains why raising the legs (shock position) can be harmful for unconscious heart-failure patients and what to do instead.

ruler-045.request: Create a brief patient-education scene that explains which everyday symptoms are usually harmless and not warning signs of worsening heart failure.
